UNDERSTANDING
Did you have any interesting dreams last night?

Our dreams come from a part of the brain that contains our thoughts and ==memories==. A person can have up to six dreams a night. Each one usually ==lasts== from 10 to 40 minutes. Everyone dreams, but not everyone remembers their dreams. Most people dream in color, usually with sound. And we usually dream about ourselves and the people we know.
Why Do We Dream?

Alan Siegel is a scientist who studies dreams. "[Dreams] can tell us a lot about ourselves," he says, "and can help us figure out ==problems==." Another scientist, Robert Stickgold, thinks dreams come from our memories. Stickgold says that dreaming about past events is ==useful== because it helps us learn from them.

Dream 2: You're Flying
If you dream about flying, you are probably quite happy. This is a good ==period== in your life. You may feel that other people see you as a leader.
Dream 3: You Didn't Study for a Test
This probably means you are ==worried== about an important future event. If you haven't ==prepared== for it, your dream may be telling you, "It's time to get to work!"
